newsitem.title: USA: Saxton says is expanding U.S. economic panel staff.
newsitem.headline: Saxton says is expanding U.S. economic panel staff.

text.p: U.S. Rep. Jim Saxton, the new chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, said Tuesday he has expanded the staff of the committee with former staff of the Federal Reserve, Treasury, Defense Department and other organizations.
In a statement, the New Jersey Republican also said he hoped to build on the relationship with the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, among other organizations.
Saxton said he has received an internal memo from the bureau evaluating the findings of a recent report on the Consumer Price Index.
The report, prepared by a panel led by Stanford University economist Michael Boskin, concluded the CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage points a year.
The Joint Economic Committee chairman said he will release a copy of the evaluation soon.
Saxton has been vice chairman of the committee for the past two years. The chairmanship and the vice chairmanship of the panel rotate between the House and the Senate each Congress.
